intro: Japanese uses parts of the body for character, skill and social life, and each part stands for one idea: 頭 the mind, 顔 your social face, 目 desire and attention, 口 speech and taste, 手 labour, 足 progress and money, 腹 anger, 首 your job. The literal English guess is usually wrong (顔が広い is not a wide face), so learn the idea of the part and the whole expression with its fixed particle.

skills.rule: 頭 is the mind, 顔 your social face, 目 desire and attention, 耳 what you hear about yourself, 口 speech and taste, 鼻 pride.
skills.explain:
頭: 頭に来る 'be furious', casual and strong (あの言い方には頭に来た); 頭が固い 'inflexible, set in one's ways'.

顔: 顔が広い 'know a lot of people' (a trait); 顔を出す 'show up, drop in' (an action): パーティーに少し顔を出す.

目: Xに目がない 'can't resist X'; Xに目を通す 'look over, skim X' (documents, mail).

耳: 耳が痛い 'it hits home', said of criticism you know is fair.

口: 口が堅い 'can keep a secret' (opposite 口が軽い); Xの口に合う 'suit X's taste', said of food, often お口に合うといいのですが.

鼻: 鼻が高い 'be proud', usually of your child, student or team.

English guesses go wrong: 頭に来る is not 'occur to me' (that is 頭に浮かぶ or 思いつく), 目がない is a weakness, not blindness, and 鼻が高い is pride, not snobbery.
patterns: [cause] に 頭に来る — be furious
頭が固い — inflexible
顔が広い — know many people
[event] に 顔を出す — show up, drop in
[thing] に 目がない — can't resist
[document] に 目を通す — look over
耳が痛い — criticism that hits home
口が堅い / 口が軽い — keeps / can't keep secrets
[person] の 口に合う — suits one's taste
鼻が高い — be proud (of one's own people)

examples.jp: 母[はは]は甘[あま]いものに{目[め]がない}。
週末[しゅうまつ]のパーティーに少[すこ]しだけ{顔[かお]を出[だ]します}。
examples.en: I'll drop in on the party at the weekend for a little while.

examples.jp: 田中[たなか]さんは{顔[かお]が広[ひろ]い}から、誰[だれ]か紹介[しょうかい]してくれるよ。
examples.en: Tanaka-san knows lots of people, so he'll introduce you to someone.

examples.jp: 会議[かいぎ]の前[まえ]に、この資料[しりょう]に{目[め]を通[とお]して}おいてください。
examples.en: Please look over these materials before the meeting.

examples.jp: 息子[むすこ]が大学[だいがく]に合格[ごうかく]して、{鼻[はな]が高[たか]い}です。
examples.en: My son got into university and I'm very proud.

examples.jp: 部長[ぶちょう]の注意[ちゅうい]は{耳[みみ]が痛[いた]い}けれど、その通[とお]りだ。
examples.en: The manager's criticism hurts to hear, but it's true.

contrast.vs: 頭に来る ↔ 腹が立つ
contrast.note: Both are anger. 頭に来る is sudden, blunt and casual; 腹が立つ is the everyday neutral way to say you are angry at something (Xに腹が立つ).

contrast.vs: 顔が広い ↔ 顔を出す
contrast.note: 顔が広い is a trait (many acquaintances). 顔を出す is a single action (put in an appearance somewhere).
口に合う is about food matching someone's taste, usually a guest's or in the negative: 辛すぎて口に合わない. For a general liking, use 好き.

mistakes.bad: いいアイデアが{頭[あたま]に来[き]ました}。
mistakes.good: いいアイデアが{頭[あたま]に浮[う]かびました}。
mistakes.note: 頭に来る means get angry. An idea coming to mind is 頭に浮かぶ.

mistakes.bad: 彼女[かのじょ]は{口[くち]が軽[かる]い}から、秘密[ひみつ]を話[はな]しても大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]です。
mistakes.good: 彼女[かのじょ]は{口[くち]が堅[かた]い}から、秘密[ひみつ]を話[はな]しても大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]です。
mistakes.note: Someone safe to tell a secret to is 口が堅い. 口が軽い means they will spread it.

mistakes.bad: 部長[ぶちょう]は{頭[あたま]がいい}から、新[あたら]しいやり方[かた]を認[みと]めない。
mistakes.good: 部長[ぶちょう]は{頭[あたま]が固[かた]い}から、新[あたら]しいやり方[かた]を認[みと]めない。
mistakes.note: Refusing new ideas is 頭が固い 'inflexible'. 頭がいい means clever and gives the wrong logic.

skills.tip: Name the faculty first (mind, face, desire, speech, pride), then take the body part that stands for it.

skills.rule: 手 is labour and getting things, 足 is progress and money, 腹 is anger, 腕 is skill, 首 is your job, 胸 is emotion, 肩 is taking sides.
skills.explain:
手: 手を貸す 'lend a hand'; 手が空く 'be free' from what you were doing; Xを手に入れる 'get hold of X' (intransitive: Xが手に入る).

足: Xの足を引っ張る 'hold X back, drag the team down'; 足が出る 'go over budget'.

腹: Xに腹が立つ 'be angry at X', the feeling inside; for someone else's anger say 腹を立てている.

腕: 腕がいい 'skilled', of cooks, doctors, craftspeople.

首: 首になる 'be fired', often written クビ; the person fired is the subject. The employer 首にする.

胸: 胸がいっぱい 'too moved for words'. A full stomach is お腹がいっぱい.

肩: Xの肩を持つ 'take X's side' in a dispute; it is not physical help.

Keep the direction: 手を貸す is giving help, and asking for it is 手を貸してください.
patterns: [person] に 手を貸す — lend a hand
手が空いたら — when you're free
[thing] を 手に入れる / が 手に入る — get hold of
[person / team] の 足を引っ張る — hold back
足が出る — go over budget
[cause] に 腹が立つ — be angry at
腕がいい — skilled
首になる / 首にする — be fired / fire
胸がいっぱいになる — be overcome with emotion
[person] の 肩を持つ — take someone's side

examples.jp: ちょっと{手[て]を貸[か]して}くれる？
examples.en: Can you give me a hand?

examples.jp: {手[て]が空[あ]いたら}、こっちを手伝[てつだ]ってください。
examples.en: When you're free, please help over here.

examples.jp: やっと人気[にんき]のコンサートのチケットを{手[て]に入[い]れた}。
examples.en: I finally got hold of tickets for the popular concert.

examples.jp: 旅行[りょこう]でお金[かね]を使[つか]いすぎて、{足[あし]が出[で]た}。
examples.en: I spent too much on the trip and went over budget.

examples.jp: 母[はは]はいつも弟[おとうと]の{肩[かた]を持[も]つ}。
examples.en: My mother always takes my little brother's side.

examples.jp: 卒業式[そつぎょうしき]では{胸[むね]がいっぱいになった}。
examples.en: I was overcome with emotion at the graduation ceremony.

contrast.note: 腹が立つ is the anger you feel (弟に腹が立った). 怒る is getting angry, often openly, and can also mean scold.

contrast.vs: 手に入れる ↔ 手に入る
contrast.note: A transitive pair: you 手に入れる a thing with を; the thing 手に入る with が. チケットを手に入れた = チケットが手に入った.

contrast.vs: 胸がいっぱい ↔ お腹がいっぱい
contrast.note: 胸 is the heart: moved. お腹 is the stomach: full from eating.

mistakes.bad: 私[わたし]はミスばかりして、チームの{足[あし]が出[で]た}。
mistakes.good: 私[わたし]はミスばかりして、チームの{足[あし]を引[ひ]っ張[ぱ]った}。
mistakes.note: Dragging the team down is 足を引っ張る. 足が出る means overspending a budget.

mistakes.bad: 会社[かいしゃ]は彼[かれ]を{首[くび]になった}。
mistakes.good: 会社[かいしゃ]は彼[かれ]を{首[くび]にした}。
mistakes.note: 首になる has the fired person as subject (彼は首になった). The employer firing someone is 首にする.

mistakes.bad: あの店[みせ]の料理人[りょうりにん]は{手[て]がいい}。
mistakes.good: あの店[みせ]の料理人[りょうりにん]は{腕[うで]がいい}。
mistakes.note: Skill is 腕, not 手: 腕がいい 'good at the job'.

skills.tip: Ask what the sentence is about (help, money, anger, skill, job, emotion, sides) and take the body part that owns that idea.
